The new completeness guards and real write/cleanup are correct; preserve them and all accepted requirements and unrelated work. One remaining implementation issue prevents approval: landing_control_view, search_product_link_view, search_blocker_view and product_fact_view are whole-array extract transforms. Their data is already typed and this is pure field copying; those tasks would incur unnecessary mapping generation on raw records. Replace this wiring using existing nested foreach with an empty task body and direct object exports from item fields, preserving every record and its order. Keep each view's current requires guard unchanged. For example a foreach over the existing records input can have body.tasks=[] and body.outputs=[{name: "records", value: {kind: "object", members: [{name: "text", value: {kind: "field", port: "text", items: [{kind: "item"}]}}]}}], extended with the view's actual required fields. Its records port is then the collected array; consumers can keep that port. Choose the iteration bound consistently with the declared page record bound. No mode=extract or interpretation is needed for these field projections, no JavaScript in TaskPlan, and no per-record inference.
Also search_page_bundle currently duplicates each record in both link and blocker views passed to one global selector. That consumer needs the link view's kind/tag/text/group/role/href to choose products and detect visible blockers; pass that view once, plus exact page grouping/reference if needed. Keep original complete observations and guards in source bindings. Do not send duplicate control records, raw observations, selectors or whole manifests into the global call. Preserve explicit consent, fresh post-consent capture, actual bounded per-product navigation, precise nullable observations, the real workbook writer and root browser cleanup. This is an explicit implementation revision only, without changing budgets, permissions, oracles or requirements.
